questions.q:
Statement-I : Two forces P→+Q→ and P→-Q→ where P→⊥Q→, when act at an angle θ1 each other, the magnitude of their resultant is 3P2+Q2, when they act at an angle θ2, the magnitude of their resultant becomes 2P2+Q2. This is possible only when θ1<θ2.
Statement-II : In the situation given above.
θ1=60° and θ2=90°
In the light of the above statement, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
F→1 and F→2 at θ1
Fnet 1=P2+Q2+P2+Q2+2P2+Q2cosθ1
Fnet 2=P2+Q2+P2+Q2+2P2+Q2cosθ2
If Fnet 1=3P2+Q2=2P2+Q2+2P2+Q2cosθ1
⇒ cosθ1=P2+Q22P2+Q2
⇒ θ1=60°
Fnet 2=2P2+Q2=2P2+Q2+2P2+Q2cosθ2
⇒ cosθ2=0  ⇒  θ2=90°

questions.q: A physical quantity <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi></math> is given as <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><msup><mi>b</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><mrow><mi>c</mi><msqrt><mi>d</mi></msqrt></mrow></mfrac></math>. The percentage error in the measurement of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi>c</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>d</mi></math> are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>%</mo><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>2</mn><mo>%</mo><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>3</mn><mo>%</mo></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mo>%</mo></math> respectively. The percentage error in the measurement of quantity <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi></math> will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The given quantity is P=a2b3cd.

The percentage error for a quantity can be given by the formula ∆xx×100.

Relation of the relative errors will be,

ΔPP=2Δaa+3Δbb+Δcc+12Δdd

Hence, the percentage error is calculated by substituting the values,

ΔPP×100=2×1+3×2+3+12×4=13%.

questions.q:
Statement I: If three forces F→1, F→2 and F→3 are represented by three sides of a triangle and F1→+F2→=-F→3, then these three forces are concurrent forces and satisfy the condition for equilibrium.
Statement II: A triangle made up of three forces F1→, F2→ and F3→ as its sides were taken in the same order, satisfies the condition for translatory equilibrium.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Use triangle law of vector addition, 

here, F→1+F→2+F→3=0, since net force is zero it means the body is in equilibrium so both the statements are correct.

questions.q: A physical quantity <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Q</mi></math> is found to depend on quantities <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi>c</mi></math> by the relation <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Q</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><msup><mi>b</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><msup><mi>c</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac></math>. The percentage error in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi>b</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi></math> are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo>%</mo><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>4</mn><mo>%</mo></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo>%</mo></math> respectively. Then, the percentage error in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Q</mi></math> is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given quantity is Q=a4b3c2.

The relative error in measuring Q is given by

ΔQQ=4Δaa+3Δbb+2Δcc   ...1

Hence, the required percentage error is given by

ΔQQ×100=4Δaa×100+3Δbb×100+2Δcc×100=4×3%+3×4%+2×5%=12%+12%+10%=34%

Hence option (4).

questions.q: Two resistance are given as R1=(10±0.5) Ω and R2=(15±0.5) Ω. The percentage error in the measurement of equivalent resistance when they are connected in parallel is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Equivalent resistance in parallel combination is given by
$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{1}{R_{\text {eq }}}=\frac{1}{R_1}+\frac{1}{R_2} \\
& \Rightarrow R_{\text {eq }}=\frac{R_1 R_2}{R_1+R_2}=\frac{10 \times 15}{10+15}=6
\end{aligned}$
Differentiating both sides, we get
$\begin{aligned} & \frac{\Delta R_{\text {eq }}}{\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{eq}}^2}=\frac{\Delta \mathrm{R}_1}{\mathrm{R}_1^2}+\frac{\Delta \mathrm{R}_2}{\mathrm{R}_2^2} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{\Delta \mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{eq}}}{\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{eq}}}=\left(\frac{\Delta \mathrm{R}_1}{\mathrm{R}_1^2}+\frac{\Delta \mathrm{R}_2}{\mathrm{R}_2^2}\right) \mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{eq}} \\ & =\left(\frac{0.5}{100}+\frac{0.5}{225}\right) \cdot 6=\left(\frac{6 \times 0.5}{25}\right)\left(\frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{9}\right)=\frac{13}{300} \\ & \frac{\Delta \mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{eq}}}{\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{eq}}} \times 100=\frac{13}{3}=4.33 \%\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The maximum error in the measurement of resistance, current and time for which current flows in an electrical circuit are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>%</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>%</mo></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo>%</mo></math> respectively. The maximum percentage error in the detection of the dissipated heat will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Heat generated through resistance is given by, H=i2Rt

Therefore, the percentage error in the calculation can be found by,

⇒ΔHH×100=2×Δii×100+ΔRR×100+Δtt×100

⇒ΔHH×100=4%+1%+3%

⇒ΔHH×100=8%

questions.q: If the percentage errors in measuring the length and the diameter of a wire are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>%</mo></math> each. The percentage error in measuring its resistance will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Resistance of the wire in terms of the diameter can be written as, R=ρLπd24

Hence, percentage error relation will be, ∆RR×100=∆LL×100+2∆dd×100

Given: ∆LL=0.1% and ∆dd=0.1%

Therefore, ∆RR=0.3%

questions.q: Two particles are located at equal distance from origin. The position vectors of those are represented by $\bar{A}=2 \hat{i}+3 n \hat{j}+2 \hat{k}$ and $\bar{B}=2 \hat{i}-2 \hat{j}+4 p \hat{k}$, respectively. If both the vectors are at right angle to each other, the value of $\mathrm{n}^{-1}$ is _____ .
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \overrightarrow{\mathrm{A}} \cdot \overrightarrow{\mathrm{B}}=0 \\ & 4-6 \mathrm{n}+8 \mathrm{p}=0 \\ & |\overrightarrow{\mathrm{~A}}|=|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{B}}| \\ & 4+9 \mathrm{n}^2+4=4+4+16 \mathrm{p}^2 \\ & 9 \mathrm{n}^2=16 \mathrm{p}^2 \\ & \mathrm{P}=+\frac{3}{4} \mathrm{n} \\ & 4-6 \mathrm{n} \pm 6 \mathrm{n}=0 \\ & 12 \mathrm{n}=4 \\ & \mathrm{n}=\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: For three vectors $\vec{A}=(-x \hat{i}-6 \hat{j}-2 \hat{k}), \vec{B}=(-\hat{i}+4 \hat{j}+3 \hat{k})$ and $\vec{C}=(-8 \hat{i}-\hat{j}+3 \hat{k})$, if $\vec{A} \cdot(\vec{B} \times \vec{C})=0$, then value of $x$ is _________
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \vec{B} \times \vec{C}=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}\hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ -1 & 4 & 3 \\ -8 & -1 & 3\end{array}\right|=15 \hat{i}-21 \hat{j}+33 \hat{k} \\ & \vec{A} \cdot(\vec{B} \times \vec{C})=(-x \hat{i}-6 \hat{j}-2 \hat{k}) \cdot(15 \hat{i}-21 \hat{j}+33 \hat{k}) \\ & 0=-15 x+126-66 \\ & 15 x=60 \\ & x=4\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If the projection of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mover><mi>i</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><mover><mi>j</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mover><mi>k</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></math> on <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mover><mi>i</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mover><mi>j</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>+</mo><mi>α</mi><mover><mi>k</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></math> is zero. Then, the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>α</mi></math> will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given here:

a→=2i^+4j^-2k^ and b→=i^+2j^+αk^

Now, a→·b→=0, as a→ should be perpendicular to b→.

∴  2×1+4×2-2×α=0 

∴  α=5

questions.q: In an experiment of measuring the refractive index of a glass slab using travelling microscope in physics lab, a student measures real thickness of the glass slab as <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>25</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math> and apparent thickness of the glass slab at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>00</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math>.
